input_interpretation.assumption: The TIFF stack is a reconstructed volumetric scan, likely XCT or micro-CT. If it is only an optical surface scan, internal void detection is not physically supported.

recommended_workflow.primary_strategy: Register the STL-derived solid occupancy volume to the scan, segment the scan into material/background, and compute voxel-wise disagreement maps.
steps: Read TIFF slices with voxel spacing, orientation, and intensity calibration preserved.
Crop to the specimen bounding box and resample the STL and scan to a common voxel grid.
Repair or validate the STL as a watertight manifold before voxelization.
Perform rigid registration using coarse principal-axis alignment followed by overlap-based or surface-based refinement.
Create a binary CAD occupancy mask and optionally a signed-distance field.
Segment scan material using robust thresholding, local background correction, or a learned model.
Compute disagreement classes: expected material but scanned void, expected void but scanned material, and scan anomalies inside expected material.
Remove isolated noise using connected-component size filtering and 3D morphology.
Extract defect volume, centroid, bounding box, connectedness, aspect ratio, roundness, maximum dimension, and orientation.
Validate detection limits using known resolution, voxel size, contrast-to-noise ratio, and synthetic defects inserted into the registered CAD volume.

methods.name: CAD-to-scan occupancy difference
methods.description: Voxelize the STL into a binary solid mask and compare it with a segmented scan mask. The difference map directly localizes missing material, excess material, blocked channels, and geometric discontinuities.

applicability.discontinuities: High for volumetric gaps or connected lack-of-fusion regions; limited for cracks thinner than the scan resolution.
applicability.missing_features: High when the missing feature is represented in the STL and the scan segmentation is reliable.
applicability.internal_voids: Moderate to high for voids inside expected material; requires sufficient X-ray contrast and registration accuracy.

limitations: Registration errors can look like defects, especially near surfaces and thin walls.
Binary thresholding loses grayscale information and can merge small voids with noise.
STL tessellation and non-watertight geometry can introduce voxelization artifacts.
references: du Plessis et al., Quality Control of a Laser Additive Manufactured Medical Implant by X-Ray Tomography, 2016, https://doi.org/10.1089/3dp.2016.0012
Yao et al., Fully automated registration of 3D CT data to CAD model for surface deviation measurement, 2019, https://doi.org/10.3233/XST-190561

methods.name: Signed-distance-field comparison
methods.description: Represent both nominal CAD and scanned geometry with signed distance fields. Threshold the absolute distance difference rather than relying only on binary occupancy.

applicability.discontinuities: High for geometric deviations and surface-adjacent discontinuities.
applicability.missing_features: High for missing or displaced channels, ribs, holes, and other designed features.
applicability.internal_voids: Moderate; direct occupancy comparison is generally better for fully internal pores.

advantages: More tolerant of small registration and surface discretization errors than raw binary XOR.
Provides signed directionality: inward loss versus outward excess.
Naturally supports distance-based defect severity metrics.
references: Chand et al., Deep Learning based 3D Volume Correlation for Additive Manufacturing Using High-Resolution Industrial XCT, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07757
Comparative Evaluation of Voxel and Mesh Representations for Digital Defect Detection in Construction-Scale Additive Manufacturing, 2026, https://www.mdpi.com/2075-5309/16/4/805

methods.name: Direct volumetric scan anomaly detection
methods.description: Segment material and identify anomalous low-intensity or high-contrast voxel clusters directly within the scan, without requiring CAD.

applicability.discontinuities: High for pores, lack-of-fusion regions, inclusions, and other intensity-visible anomalies.
applicability.missing_features: Low to moderate unless the nominal feature geometry is also available.
applicability.internal_voids: High when voids have sufficient contrast and are larger than the effective detection limit.

implementation_pattern: Estimate material/background thresholds globally or per slice.
Apply local background correction for beam hardening and intensity drift.
Use multiscale 3D filters or morphological top-hat operations.
Threshold saliency responses and label connected components.
Filter components by physical volume, aspect ratio, and location within the CAD material mask.
references: Petrich and Reutzel, Automated Defect Recognition for Additive Manufactured Parts Using Machine Perception and Visual Saliency, 2023, https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/automated-defect-recognition-for-additive-manufactured-parts-usin/
Standard method for microCT-based additive manufacturing quality control: Porosity analysis, 2018, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6159003/

methods.name: 3D connected-component and morphology analysis
methods.description: After segmentation, label 26-connected defect regions and classify them using geometric descriptors.

applicability.discontinuities: High for connected gaps and irregular lack-of-fusion regions.
applicability.internal_voids: High for isolated pores and connected porosity networks.

useful_features: overlap with expected CAD material or feature regions
references: Poudel et al., Feature-based volumetric defect classification in metal additive manufacturing, Nature Communications, 2022, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-34122-x
methods.evidence: Using multiple morphological descriptors, rather than one or two thresholds, was reported to classify lack-of-fusion, gas-entrapped pores, and keyholes with over 98 percent decision-tree accuracy and over 99 percent neural-network accuracy.

methods.name: 3D U-Net or other volumetric neural segmentation
methods.description: Train a 3D CNN to segment defect voxels directly from scan volumes.

applicability.discontinuities: High if representative labeled examples exist.
applicability.missing_features: Moderate; requires CAD-aware labels or synthetic missing-feature examples.
applicability.internal_voids: High for complex appearance variation, provided training data cover the scan domain.

tradeoffs: Strong performance but high memory use.
Requires labeled volumetric data and careful handling of severe class imbalance.
Patch-based inference is required for large TIFF stacks.
Synthetic defect generation can reduce labeling cost but may create domain shift.
references: Wong et al., Automatic Volumetric Segmentation of Additive Manufacturing Defects with 3D U-Net, AAAI, 2021, https://eil.stanford.edu/sites/g/files/sbiybj34491/files/media/file/am_3dunet_aaai.pdf

Bimrose et al., Detecting and classifying hidden defects in additively manufactured parts using deep learning and X-ray computed tomography, Journal of Intelligent Manufacturing, 2025, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10845-024-02416-0
Automatic detection of hidden defects and qualification of additively manufactured parts using X-ray computed tomography and computer vision, 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mfglet.2024.09.147

discontinuities.best_signal: Localized scan-background regions inside expected CAD material, especially elongated or irregular connected components.

missing_features.best_signal: Expected CAD void or channel occupied by scan material, or expected CAD solid absent from the scan.
missing_features.important_check: Differentiate true missing features from scan segmentation failure, partial-volume effects, and registration drift.

internal_voids.best_signal: Low-intensity connected regions enclosed by expected material.
internal_voids.important_check: Use scan-resolution and detectability estimates; small or irregular defects can be missed or have their volume underestimated.

recommended_stack: SciPy ndimage for filtering, distance transforms, morphology, and connected components
Dask or Zarr for out-of-core TIFF-stack processing
CuPy or PyTorch only when GPU memory is available
principles: Process only the registered specimen ROI rather than the full scanner volume.
Store binary masks as uint8 or bool; store intensities and distance fields as float32.
Use slab-wise processing along the z-axis with overlap margins at least as large as the largest filter radius.
Use separable 3D filters as sequential 1D convolutions instead of dense 3D kernels.
Use vectorized boolean operations for occupancy differences and avoid Python loops over voxels.
Use sparse or run-length representations for highly sparse defect masks.
For connected components across slabs, merge labels touching adjacent slab boundaries using a union-find structure.
Compute morphology descriptors only for candidate components, not for every voxel.
Use distance transforms and nearest-neighbor searches on cropped boundary bands rather than allocating full pairwise distance matrices.
Use patch-based neural inference with overlap and tiled aggregation if deep learning is required.

complexity_guidance.occupancy_comparison: O(N) time and approximately one to three bytes per voxel for masks.
complexity_guidance.distance_field: O(N) for standard Euclidean distance transforms, but process in chunks when N is large.
complexity_guidance.neural_segmentation: Memory is dominated by feature maps; use small overlapping 3D patches and mixed precision.

resolution_and_validation.minimum_detection_warning: A defect represented by fewer than approximately 2 to 3 voxels across its smallest dimension is unreliable and may disappear after reconstruction, interpolation, or thresholding.
resolution_and_validation.evidence: A recent registered XCT dataset reported an approximate flaw detection limit of 50 to 75 micrometers, corresponding to about 2 to 3 voxels, while a controlled XCT study showed that irregular lack-of-fusion features are lost more readily than near-spherical pores as voxel size increases.
references: A co-registered in-situ and ex-situ dataset from wire arc additive manufacturing process, 2025, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04638-0
Non-destructive detection of critical defects in additive manufacturing, 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11861637/
validation_protocol: Measure voxel spacing and estimate effective spatial resolution.
Insert synthetic spherical, elongated, crack-like, and missing-feature defects into the CAD volume.
Forward-model or intensity-blend synthetic defects into defect-free scans when possible.
Evaluate detection probability versus defect size, shape, orientation, and depth.
Report precision, recall, localization error, volumetric bias, and false positives near boundaries.
Perform sensitivity analysis over segmentation threshold, registration tolerance, and minimum component size.

overall_recommendation.preferred_baseline: Use a two-stage hybrid pipeline: robust scan segmentation plus registered STL occupancy comparison, followed by 3D connected-component morphology.
overall_recommendation.why: It directly addresses missing features and internal voids, uses the available STL prior, is substantially more memory efficient than a full 3D CNN, and provides interpretable defect locations and measurements.
overall_recommendation.when_to_add_deep_learning: Add patch-based 3D U-Net or synthetic-data ViT classification only if thresholding and morphology cannot separate defects from artifacts or if a sufficiently representative labeled dataset is available.
overall_recommendation.confidence: High for volumetric voids and CAD-defined missing features when scan resolution and registration are adequate; moderate for thin cracks and irregular discontinuities near the detectability limit.
